package_info.package_versions: Orion Platform versions released between March 2020 and June 2020 (exact versions not specified in the report)
package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised during the build process to include the SUNBURST (Solorigate) backdoor, which enabled remote attacker control over customer environments. The malicious code was inserted into a core DLL, digitally signed, and distributed via official updates, resulting in widespread downstream compromise and unauthorized remote access.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (DLL load during Orion service startup)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code checks for signs of a legitimate environment, waits a random interval to evade detection, initiates outbound HTTP/S connections to attacker-controlled C2 domains, receives remote commands, and executes them, resulting in unauthorized remote control of the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code introduces a covert backdoor that establishes outbound connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure and executes arbitrary remote commands, which is highly abnormal for legitimate IT management software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Orion DLLs should not initiate outbound network connections to unknown or untrusted domains, nor should they execute code or commands received from external sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: While remote management tools may contact official update servers for legitimate purposes, they do not connect to arbitrary external domains or execute attacker-supplied code received over the network.
key_indicators: Outbound HTTP/S connections from core DLLs to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com and subdomains)
Randomized execution delays before network activity to evade detection
Execution of remote commands received from C2 infrastructure
Obfuscated or benign-appearing code embedded within a digitally signed core DLL
Modification of SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with code not present in official releases

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to SolarWinds build infrastructure and injects malicious code into the Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in official software builds.

attack_chain.action: Malicious DLL is digitally signed and distributed via official SolarWinds update channels.
attack_chain.leads_to: Customers download and install trojanized updates.

attack_chain.action: When Orion services start, the malicious DLL loads and executes the backdoor logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor establishes contact with attacker C2 infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: Backdoor receives and executes attacker commands, enabling lateral movement, data exfiltration, or further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full attacker control of victim environments.

behavioral_signatures: Core DLLs (e.g., SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll) initiating outbound HTTP/S connections to untrusted or known malicious domains
Randomized delays (hours to days) before initial network activity after service startup
Execution of remote commands or scripts received over HTTP/S from external infrastructure
Digitally signed binaries exhibiting unexpected network or process creation behaviors
Presence of obfuscated or non-standard code blocks within core SolarWinds DLLs
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (hashes matching known trojanized SUNBURST versions)
Unexpected changes or additions in core DLLs between official SolarWinds releases
Presence of digitally signed DLLs with code not present in verified clean versions
network_indicators: Outbound connections to avsvmcloud.com and related subdomains (known SUNBURST C2 domains)
Unusual HTTP/S traffic from Orion servers to external IPs or domains not associated with SolarWinds
DNS queries for attacker-controlled domains as listed in SUNBURST IOCs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected outbound HTTP/S connections from Orion servers, especially to known SUNBURST C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com). Compare hashes of SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll against known-good versions to detect unauthorized modifications. Analyze process behavior for randomized delays before network activity and execution of remote commands. Alert on digitally signed binaries exhibiting suspicious network or command execution activity. Correlate network, file, and behavioral indicators to identify compromise.
